articles.title: Trump's newest blame-game play enrages: 'District isn’t Trump’s personal property!'
articles.description: The Trump administration — fresh off a failed attempt to blame vandals for botched work on the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool — has tried once again to dodge responsibility and enraged locals in the process. Trump's latest political jab spurred one D.C. local to snap off a photo and send it to Newsweek , along with a vent over her frustration. The photo shows that the National Park Service has posted a sign on the monument blaming previous administrations for neglecting the site, claiming "more than half of the 58 water supply ports were so clogged that they were deemed nonfunctioning." The sign read: "The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has been partially refilled to allow National Park Service staff and contractors to flush the pool's piping system for the first time in more than a decade." It also told the public that the flushing process could "temporarily discolor the water as buildup in the pipes is cleaned out." Suzanne Garwood told Newsweek she was livid. "They just took down the extended fencing from the Fourth so this is the first time we could get that close to the pool in weeks," Garwood fumed. "The East Wing, the Kennedy Center, the Arts of War and Peace, and the Pool. Next up is the Arch and destroying our cherry trees for a golf course. The District isn’t Trump’s personal property."

articles.title: Schedule for 3rd phase of AJK polls revised over law and order concerns
articles.description: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Election Commission on Friday revised the schedule for the third phase of elections in the region, saying polling in seven of the 11 constituencies of Poonch Division had been postponed due to concerns over the law and order situation in those areas. However, the electoral process will go ahead as planned on August 10 in the other four constituencies, the Election Commission said in a press release. These included the division’s Bagh and Haveli districts. Poonch Division comprises 11 constituencies — three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch and two in Sudhnoti. Amid tensions between protesters and the authorities, elections are being held across the region in three phases , with those in Mirpur and Muzaffarabad divisions held on July 27 and August 2, respectively. The third phase in Poonch division is set for August 10. More to follow
